findings: The complete-entry fake matches delegate-preflight argv without -i although production uses -i.
Native delegate-result metadata extraction does not use the same normalized tool name as call classification; the positive fixture must also use the actual unprefixed local delegate name.
A preflight assertion treats argv[10] as the Python source; with the exact production argv it is -c and the source is argv[11].

prior_source_review.preserved_additional_hold: The earlier header set comparison accepted an unknown field when an optional field was absent. Required-subset and allowed-superset checks were repaired and the inline reader pin updated before this review.

root_decision: Repair production name normalization and the complete-entry transport fixture, freeze four files again, and obtain independent source admission before the first execution.
evidence_boundaries: UID/GID and filesystem facts in the offline transport are synthetic, not actual container UID/DAC proof.
The cleanup response is a synthetic scoped transport result; it does not prove a daemon MAC or a native child close ACK.
The complete-entry fake retains production main, native decoding and identity/result validation algorithms.
